name: Consultant
title: Free Consulting Invoice Template
description: A free consulting invoice template that separates professional fees from expenses, with hours, rates and the engagement named. Download a PDF for free.
summary: Professional fees and expenses in separate, subtotalled sections, with the engagement named.
intro: Fees and expenses in separate sections with their own subtotals, the engagement named in the side column, and nothing a finance team would have to ask about.
explanation: Consulting clients usually book fees and reimbursable expenses to different budget lines, and their accounts payable team needs to see them apart. A single list mixing a strategy workshop with a train ticket gets sent back.

This template divides the invoice into Professional fees and Expenses, each subtotalled. Fees show hours and an hourly rate; expenses are listed at cost. The engagement name, your details and the payment terms sit in a ruled side column in Garamond, which reads as the formal document it is.

It suits management and operations consultants, advisers, coaches, interim executives and independent researchers. For retainers billed as a headline amount, the [Executive template](/invoice-templates/executive/) is an alternative.
fieldsTitle: What to put on a consulting invoice

fields.name: Engagement
fields.text: The engagement or statement of work it falls under: “Q3 operations review”. Add the PO or contract reference if there is one.

fields.name: Professional fees
fields.text: Each activity with hours and rate: analysis, interviews, workshops, reporting. Day rates work too: days as quantity.

fields.name: Expenses
fields.text: Travel, accommodation, materials or third-party costs, at cost, with the date or destination. Say receipts are attached.

fields.name: Period
fields.text: The dates the invoice covers, in the engagement name or the notes, for monthly or phase billing.

fields.name: Tax ID
fields.text: Your tax or VAT number where clients need it; in the US, a client may ask for a W-9 before the first payment.

fields.name: Payment terms
fields.text: Net 30 is common for corporate clients. Give wire or ACH details in full.

steps.title: Open the example
steps.text: Customize this invoice opens a consulting invoice with fees and expenses in the generator.

steps.title: Fees, then expenses
steps.text: Add each activity under Professional fees with its hours, then each cost under Expenses. Subtotals appear when a section has more than one line.

steps.title: Name the engagement
steps.text: Enter the engagement and any PO number. Choose terms; the due date follows.

steps.title: Attach receipts and send
steps.text: Download the PDF and send it with the expense receipts to accounts payable.

faqs.q: Should consulting expenses be on the same invoice as fees?
faqs.a: They can be, as long as they are clearly separated. This template puts them in their own section with a subtotal, which is what most finance teams ask for. Some clients prefer a separate expense invoice; follow their process.

faqs.q: Should I bill hourly or a day rate?
faqs.a: Bill the way your proposal priced the work. For a day rate, enter days as the quantity and your day rate as the rate; the column heading still reads Hours, so say “days” in the description.
Usually not; consulting expenses are commonly billed at cost with receipts. If your contract allows an administrative fee, show it as its own line.

faqs.q: How do I invoice a retainer?
faqs.a: One line for the period (“Advisory retainer — October”) with a quantity of 1. Add any work outside the retainer as separate fee lines.
